cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to Israel, and now he turns to war. Picture it: you look across the field and see horses, chariots and an army bigger than yours. Friend, I'd already be hiding behind my own mustache.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel they don't need to be afraid of an army bigger than theirs.
Horses, chariots and a bigger army on the other side. Why shouldn't Israel be afraid?

answers.text: The LORD their God is with them
Their swords are stronger than chariots
Their enemies will run away first

cards.text: And Moses names exactly who's with them: the LORD who brought them out of Egypt. Then, right before the battle, somebody comes forward to address the army.

cards.question: Israel is about to go into battle. Who comes forward to address the army?
Before the battle, the priest tells the soldiers it's fine to be terrified as long as they keep marching.
The priest tells the army the LORD their God goes with them to ___ for them against their enemies.

cards.text: The priest closes strong: the LORD gives the victory. Then the officers address the army, starting with, "Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it?"

cards.question: What do the officers say about a man who built a new house and hasn't dedicated it?
The officers send the man with the new house home because it might fall apart without him.

cards.text: Here's the officers' real reason: he may die in battle, and another man would dedicate that house. You do all the building, and somebody else cuts the ribbon.
Same goes for a man who planted a vineyard and hasn't begun to enjoy its fruit, or another man enjoys it. Imagine baking the perfect batch all night, and then somebody else eats EVERY cookie.

cards.question: One more man gets sent home: a man pledged to a woman who hasn't ___ her yet.

cards.text: Then the officers speak further: "Is any man afraid or fainthearted?" Friend, if they asked me, I'd be halfway home before they finished the question.

cards.question: The officers tell any man who's afraid or fainthearted to stay and prove himself in the battle.
Why do the officers send the afraid and fainthearted man home?

answers.text: So his brothers' hearts won't melt like his
So he can guard the empty houses back home
So he can pray for the army while it fights

cards.text: The officers are done talking. I bet the army's looking a little smaller now, but there's one more step before anybody marches.

cards.question: When the officers have finished addressing the army, they appoint ___ to lead it.

cards.text: Now Moses moves from the army to the cities. Israel marches up to fight a city, swords ready, and Moses says hold on, something comes first.

cards.question: When Israel approaches a city to fight against it, what must they do first?
If the city accepts the offer of peace and opens its gates, what happens to its people?

cards.text: But not every city says yes. Some turn the offer down flat and wage war against Israel instead.

cards.question: When a city refuses peace and wages war, Moses says Israel is to lay siege to it.

cards.text: When the LORD delivers that city into Israel's hand, every male is put to the sword. Israel may take the women, children, livestock and all the spoil as plunder.

cards.question: Moses says this is how Israel treats the cities that are far away from them.

cards.text: The cities of the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance get a different command. There, Moses says, Israel must not leave alive anything that breathes.

cards.question: Moses names the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. These are the far-away cities he talked about before.
Why must Israel devote those nations to complete destruction?

answers.text: So they can't teach Israel their detestable ways
So Israel can take all of their silver and gold
So they can't attack Israel's cities from behind

cards.text: Now picture a long siege, Israel camped outside a city for an extended time. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, so I know long waits, and out there the only scenery is the trees.

cards.question: During a long siege, Moses tells Israel to cut down the fruit trees around the city.
Moses says not to destroy the fruit trees, because Israel can ___ their fruit.

cards.text: Then Moses asks, "Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?" Friend, no tree in history ever started a fight.

cards.question: During the siege, which trees does Moses say Israel may destroy?

answers.text: Trees they know don't bear fruit
The tallest trees near the walls
Any tree the city planted itself

cards.text: Those trees build the siege works against the city until it falls. And friend, Moses isn't done preaching yet.

findings.problem: The joke 'I'd be halfway home before they finished the question' tells the baker that afraid men head home. That gives away card 15, whose wrong answer is that they stay, and it also points to card 16's setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'told' doesn't fit the blank the way the other answers do. 'Hasn't told her yet' leaves out what he told her, so it reads as filler next to 'married' and 'met.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says 'those nations,' which points back to the nations named on card 9. That card isn't on screen anymore, so the question needs to say who they are, such as the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Those trees build the siege works' makes the trees the ones doing the building, and it drops the permission. Verse 20 says Israel may destroy non-fruit trees and use them to build siege works.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Every male is put to the sword' tells the command in verse 13 as an event that happens. The text gives it as a law: 'you must put every male to the sword.' The same card then says what Israel 'may take,' so the card mixes a command and a permission without showing which is which.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
